thread:
kevin: Quick follow-up from the authn/authz sync. Prototype idea: embed a compact \"intent\" claim in API key metadata so the edge can cheaply fast-path well-known high-volume calls (e.g., vector ingest). Not a replacement for RBAC, just a perf hint.

tara: Concern: any client-side value is forgeable. How do we ensure gateway trusts it?

sam: plan is to sign the metadata blob server-side (HMAC) at issuance. Gateway verifies signature via a KMS-wrapped key. Signature field is tiny and verification is cheap.

olga: We should scope intents strictly. Proposal: 10 canonical intents max. New intent requests require a short justification + approver. Otherwise we end up with 100 one-off intents.

kevin: Agreed. Also add an intent risk tier (LOW/MED/HIGH) which drives default fail-policy and audit level.

tara: Enforcement model? Gateway only short-circuits on explicit allow for route+intent. Otherwise it forwards to full authz service. Downstream services still authoritative for final decisions.

sam: Migration suggestion: 1) Start advisory: gateway reads key, attaches X-RW-Intent for telemetry only for 3 weeks. 2) Collect mismatch metrics (intent allowed vs authz result). 3) Enable opt-in enforcement for LOW intents on specific routes. 4) Expand as confidence grows.

olga: Revocation: we need a fast revocation cache. If a key is blacklisted, gateway cache should evict in <= 30s. Push invalidations from authz service to edge via pubsub.

kevin: What about signature key rotation? If gateway can't verify signature due to rotation, what happens?

tara: Per-intent default behavior: LOW -> fail-open (but emit high-priority alert), MEDIUM -> fail-closed, HIGH -> fail-closed. But allow route-specific overrides. That minimizes blast radius.

sam: Logging: every time the gateway makes a allow/deny decision based on intent, emit structured event: {key_id, intent, route, decision, verifier_status}. We'll consume these in the security dashboard.

olga: SDKs: we should ship small verify_intent() helpers (py/ts) so services can verify signature and decode intent_version locally, and optionally consult registry.

kevin: Registry/versioning: include intent_version in the key metadata. When semantics change, bump version. Gateway and SDKs know how to interpret versions.

tara: Operational risks: drift between intent registry and service semantics. Add nightly job that flags intents with >5% mismatch against backend authz decisions.

sam: Also require an "audit_approval" tag for any key issued with HIGH intents (manual review). This should be enforced at issuance.

gatebot: deploy-bot: staging gateway canary image with intent-shim v0.1 deployed to cluster staging-a. Run canary tests.

olga: One more: require explicit opt-in on each high-throughput route to use intent short-circuits, documented in route config (no global auto-shortcut).

kevin: Good. I'll write a concise RFC covering: canonical list, signing scheme, intent_versioning, risk tiers, revocation flow, telemetry metrics, and rollout phases. Ping @tara @olga for reviews.

tara: I'll help with the mismatch dashboard and alerts.

sam: I'll prepare a lightweight HMAC verification sample and a short unit test matrix.

gatebot: reminder: run key rotation and revocation smoke tests in staging after shim enabled.

kevin: Thanks everyone. RFC link incoming when ready. :thumbsup:
